# ci-manager-github

**Realize GitHub-side resources from one token, and record what it made.**

A forge-ci `manager` engine.

## Why it exists

Bootstrap is a reconcile like any other. The engine that uses GitHub
declares what must exist there - workflow files, Actions secrets, enablement -
and this manager makes it so from one PAT, so a new pipeline instance needs
nothing clicked and nothing scripted.

## Tools

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `reconcile` | Realize every declared GitHub resource and return who owns it. |

## By hand

```sh
echo '{"manager":"github","resources":[{"kind":"actions-secret","name":"o/r/FACTORY_TOKEN","spec":{"repo":"o/r","secret":"FACTORY_TOKEN"}}]}' \
  | ci-manager-github reconcile
```

## In a pipeline

```yaml
engines:
  - alias: my-manager
    type: manager
    engine: "forge://github.com/alexandremahdhaoui/forge-ci/cmd/ci-manager-github@v0.1.0"
    manager: local
    spec:
      statePath: <string>
      apiBaseURL: <string>
      tokenEnv: <string>
```

## Worth knowing

It knows three kinds. `file-content` converges a file on the local
checkout to the declared content - drift included, unlike the local manager's
`file`, which keeps what exists; the pipeline's own push delivers it to the
remote. `actions-secret` seals the value of the named environment variable
(default GITHUB_TOKEN) against the repo key and puts it every reconcile - the
secrets API is write-only, so the put is the convergence. `workflow-enabled`
enables a workflow by file name; a workflow not yet on the remote reports
pending instead of failing, and the reconcile after the first push completes
it.

There is no delete path: a resource dropped from a spec stays as it is,
exactly like the local manager. It refuses a resource recorded as owned by a
different manager.

The token is read from the environment at realize time and never written to
state, actions or logs.
